---
name: concept-space-additions-map
description: Adding new rule families to arbitrary_exception_rule_prior barely moves MAP ll (~-1067); which additions were tried
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3 (2026-10-30), adding one new rule family (own Dirichlet weight) to the incumbent arbitrary_exception_rule_prior (MAP ll -1067.0):
- offset residue classes r mod k, k=3..6: -1066.7 (best; submitted as offset_progression_concepts, iter_3/candidate_0)
- same with k up to 12 or 25: -1067.2, weight -> 0
- multiples of 13..50: -1067.8; digit-sum = s: -1067.2 (weight 0.08); odd multiples/2-adic: -1067.2; decade blocks: -1067.3
After 69,9,39,21 the model still predicts 0.61 "yes" for 19 (observed 0/5), even with offset progressions in the space.
**Why:** the concept space is not the bottleneck. Remaining residuals are scattered single cells with n=5.
**How to apply:** don't spend another round on concept-space additions. See [[powers-of-2-37-misfit]].
---
name: incumbent-residual-diagnostics
description: Round-3 tests on arbitrary_exception_rule_prior (quick 300-draw NUTS lppd, incumbent -1068.1); which single changes help
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 3 (2026-10-30), iter_3/candidate_3. Incumbent is well calibrated (rescaling rule/range shares gains <1 nat); worst sets are 4,66,78,96, 31,3,1,15, 23,35,95,83 (parity+magnitude patterns).
- Helped: "odd/even within a range" concept kind (third Dirichlet kind weight ≈0.07, same Erlang width prior): lppd -1065.1 (+3). Submitted as parity_within_range_concepts.
- No help: fixed ALPHA 0.7/0.8/0.97 (all much worse; 0.9 is best), set-level max-gap penalty on ranges (-0.25), hierarchical within-family rule weights (+0.7, tau→0.1), decade-round range endpoints (-0.6).
- Too slow: per-interval (5050-column) likelihood with an exponent on range evidence — >10 min for 600 draws; keep per-size aggregation in prepare_observed.
**Why:** avoids re-running these next round.
**How to apply:** build on parity-within-range if it was admitted; see [[powers-of-2-37-misfit]].
- [Powers-of-2 / 37 misfit](powers-of-2-37-misfit.md) — exception-rule family fix, plus ideas that failed at MAP
- [Concept-space additions at MAP](concept-space-additions-map.md) — new rule families (APs, digit sums, big multiples) gain ≈0 nats
- [Incumbent residual diagnostics](incumbent-residual-diagnostics.md) — round-3 incumbent at noise floor; refinements that gave no MAP gain
- [Incumbent residual diagnostics](incumbent-residual-diagnostics.md) — round-3 tests: parity-within-range +3 lppd; ALPHA/gap/pooling/round ranges failed
---
name: powers-of-2-37-misfit
description: Incumbent family-prior models over-predict "yes" to 37 after powers-of-2 sets; splitting exception rules into own family gains ~8 nats MAP
metadata:
  type: project
---
In experiment1 (round 2, 2026-10-30), the incumbent erlang_interval_family_prior_concepts gave target 37 p≈0.35 after powers-of-2 sets; observed 0/25. Putting "powers of 2, not 32"/"or 37" in their own family raised MAP ll from -1075.5 to -1067.0 (candidate iter_2/candidate_5, arbitrary_exception_rule_prior).
Things that did NOT help at MAP: rule∩range conjunction concepts (-0.8), linear-in-log-odds response (+2 for 2 params), changing fixed noise ALPHA from 0.9.
Remaining misfit: predictions in the 0.2–0.4 band run ~0.07 too high (wide-range concepts extending beyond the examples).
**Why:** saves re-running diagnostics next round.
**How to apply:** start refinements from these residuals; see [[incumbent-residual-diagnostics]].
Round 3 (2026-10-30): gamma-width prior + exception family (iter_3/candidate_5, gamma_width_exception_family_concepts) MAP ll -1064.6 vs incumbent -1067.0 (+1 param; shape≈4.6, mean width≈53). Largest remaining per-set deviance: 4,66,78,96 (~-30, flat ~0.37 predicted, noisy data), 31,3,1,15, 23,35,95,83.

Round 3 (2026-10-30): generative "next-output probability relative to max, ^sensitivity" judgment on the incumbent learner gave MAP ll -1123 (vs -1067) — membership-probability reporting is clearly better; don't retry size-principle-on-target readouts.
140 experiment1/model_loop/models/parity_within_range_concepts.py

"""Refinement of arbitrary_exception_rule_prior: Bayesian concept learning over
45 rules (family-organised prior; "powers of 2 except 32"/"plus 37" are their
own kind), all intervals of 1..100 with an Erlang prior over width, examples
drawn from the concept with probability 0.9 (size principle) and from 1..100
otherwise, "yes" = posterior probability that the concept contains the target.
The single change: people also entertain a conjunctive kind of concept, "odd
(or even) numbers within a range", with its own inferred plausibility and the
same width preference as plain ranges. The three kinds (rules, ranges, parity
within a range) share prior mass by an inferred Dirichlet weight, so after
4,66,78,96 large even numbers are accepted and small even ones rejected.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt
from scipy.special import logsumexp

ALPHA = 0.9
NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


_RULES = rule_concepts()
RULE_NAMES, RULES = list(_RULES), list(_RULES.values())
N_RULES = len(RULES)
INTERVALS = [list(range(m, n + 1)) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]
PARITY_RANGES = [[n for n in c if n % 2 == p] for p in (1, 0) for c in INTERVALS]
MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES + INTERVALS + PARITY_RANGES], dtype="float64")
EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * MEMBERSHIP / np.maximum(MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True), 1) + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK[MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1) == 0] = -1e4  # empty concepts are impossible
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = MEMBERSHIP[:N_RULES]
INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP = MEMBERSHIP[N_RULES:]
_SPAN = np.array([len(c) for c in INTERVALS] * 3) - 1
INTERVAL_SIZE_IDX = _SPAN + 100 * np.repeat([0, 1, 1], len(INTERVALS))  # span class; parity ranges share 100..199
SIZES = np.arange(1, 101, dtype="float64")
LOG_N_OF_SIZE = np.log(101.0 - SIZES)  # number of intervals of each size

def rule_family(name):
    if name.startswith("powers of 2,"):  # a rule with an arbitrary exception
        return 7
    if name in ("odd", "even"):
        return 0
    if name == "primes":
        return 1
    if name in ("squares", "cubes"):
        return 2
    if name.startswith("powers"):
        return 3
    if name.startswith("multiples"):
        return 4
    if name.startswith("ends in"):
        return 5
    return 6


FAMILY = np.array([rule_family(n) for n in RULE_NAMES])
N_FAMILIES = FAMILY.max() + 1
FAMILY_SIZE = np.bincount(FAMILY)

# All intervals of one size share their prior, so prepare_observed sums each
# set's interval likelihood within every size (parameter-free) and records, per
# size, the share of that evidence from intervals containing each target.

with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_log_lik = pm.Data("rule_log_lik", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))  # (sets, rules)
    size_log_evidence = pm.Data("size_log_evidence", np.zeros((1, 200)))  # (sets, sizes): log sum_j P(D|j)
    cell_set = pm.Data("cell_set", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # (cells,)
    cell_rule_member = pm.Data("cell_rule_member", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))  # (cells, rules)
    cell_size_member = pm.Data("cell_size_member", np.zeros((1, 200)))  # (cells, sizes)
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # (trials,)
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    kind = pm.Dirichlet("kind_weights", a=np.full(3, 2.0))  # rules, ranges, odd/even within a range
    sigma = pm.LogNormal("sigma", mu=np.log(15.0), sigma=1.0)  # Erlang scale of interval width
    family_weights = pm.Dirichlet("family_weights", a=np.full(N_FAMILIES, 2.0))
    rule_log_prior = pt.log(family_weights)[FAMILY] - np.log(FAMILY_SIZE[FAMILY])

    log_size_prior = np.log(SIZES) - SIZES / sigma
    log_size_prior = log_size_prior - pt.logsumexp(log_size_prior)
    log_per_interval = pt.concatenate([pt.log(kind[1]) + log_size_prior - LOG_N_OF_SIZE,
                                       pt.log(kind[2]) + log_size_prior - LOG_N_OF_SIZE - np.log(2.0)])

    log_rules = pt.log(kind[0]) + rule_log_prior[None, :] + rule_log_lik
    log_sizes = log_per_interval[None, :] + size_log_evidence
    log_joint = pt.concatenate([log_rules, log_sizes], axis=1)
    posterior = pt.exp(log_joint - pt.logsumexp(log_joint, axis=1, keepdims=True))
    cell_post = posterior[cell_set]
    in_concept = ((cell_post[:, :N_RULES] * cell_rule_member).sum(axis=1)
                  + (cell_post[:, N_RULES:] * cell_size_member).sum(axis=1))

    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(in_concept[row_cell], 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def prepare_observed(rows):
    """Rows carry `number_set` ("16,8", in presented order), `target` and `rating`."""
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    set_log_lik = np.stack([EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK[:, np.array(s) - 1].sum(axis=1) for s in unique])
    n_sets = len(unique)
    size_ev = np.zeros((n_sets, 200))
    size_member = np.zeros((n_sets, 200, 100))
    for i in range(n_sets):
        ll = set_log_lik[i, N_RULES:]
        for L in range(200):
            sel = INTERVAL_SIZE_IDX == L
            ev = logsumexp(ll[sel])
            size_ev[i, L] = ev
            size_member[i, L] = np.exp(ll[sel] - ev) @ INTERVAL_MEMBERSHIP[sel]
    keys = [(index[s], int(r["target"])) for s, r in zip(sets, rows)]
    cells = list(dict.fromkeys(keys))
    cell_index = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(cells)}
    cell_s = np.array([c[0] for c in cells], dtype="int64")
    cell_t = np.array([c[1] - 1 for c in cells], dtype="int64")
    return {
        "rule_log_lik": set_log_lik[:, :N_RULES],
        "size_log_evidence": size_ev,
        "cell_set": cell_s,
        "cell_rule_member": RULE_MEMBERSHIP[:, cell_t].T.copy(),
        "cell_size_member": np.clip(size_member[cell_s, :, cell_t], 0.0, 1.0),
        "row_cell": np.array([cell_index[k] for k in keys], dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }

"""Refinement of parity_within_range_concepts: the single change is that the
prior over range width (plain ranges and parity-within-a-range alike) is a gamma
distribution L^(k-1) exp(-L k / mu) with shape k and mean mu both inferred,
instead of a fixed-shape Erlang, so people may expect ranges of a sharply
characteristic width. Otherwise as the incumbent, itself a refinement of
arbitrary_exception_rule_prior: Bayesian concept learning over
45 rules (family-organised prior; "powers of 2 except 32"/"plus 37" are their
own kind), all intervals of 1..100 with an Erlang prior over width, examples
drawn from the concept with probability 0.9 (size principle) and from 1..100
otherwise, "yes" = posterior probability that the concept contains the target.
The single change: people also entertain a conjunctive kind of concept, "odd
(or even) numbers within a range", with its own inferred plausibility and the
same width preference as plain ranges. The three kinds (rules, ranges, parity
within a range) share prior mass by an inferred Dirichlet weight, so after
4,66,78,96 large even numbers are accepted and small even ones rejected.
"""

content.text:
I've written the candidate for this slot, `gamma_width_parity_range_concepts`, and it passes the admission check (`OK`). Novelty against the other models and full convergence weren't checked, since the check doesn't cover them.

**The change:** I kept the incumbent `parity_within_range_concepts` as it is: rules with a family-organised prior, exception rules as their own kind, plain ranges, "odd/even within a range" concepts, and the size principle. The one change, taken from `gamma_width_exception_family_concepts`, is how wide people expect a range to be. The fixed-shape Erlang prior is replaced by a gamma prior whose sharpness and typical width are both inferred. It applies to plain and parity-restricted ranges alike, so people can expect ranges of one sharply characteristic width.

**Why this change:** The critique found no significant discrepancy in the incumbent, so I had no failure to target directly. Instead I combined the two improvements that each helped in round 3 and have not yet been tried together. My notes recorded the gamma width prior raising the fitted log-likelihood by about 2.4 nats on the exception-rule model, and the parity-within-range concepts improving fit by about 3. The new model has one extra parameter (the gamma shape; the Erlang scale becomes a mean width).

**Results so far:** The 100-draw smoke fit gave a log-likelihood of −1066.8 and the check took about 75 s. That is not yet evidence that it beats the incumbent: it's a short single-chain run, and the full fit will decide.

**Risk:** another candidate this round could make the same combination. None of the other candidate folders had any files when I looked.

I also corrected a docstring line copied from the incumbent that still said "Erlang prior". I added a note about this round to the memory directory.

Files are in `iter_4/candidate_3/`:
- `hypothesis.md`
- `model_name.txt`
- `candidate.py`
